scope: RN/RAN/RNN medium and lower naval hulls relevant to Eastern Fleet and the January 1944 reinforcement passage; separates existing station assets, true January arrivals, transient ferries and later reinforcements.
authority_note: No CURRENT execution authority is changed. Dated future arrivals are trace-locked historical baselines only unless/until the discussion clock reaches them without a causal Branch interruption.
branch_rules_applied: Preserve named historical movement unless a Branch divergence causally intersects it; do not delete a named arrival merely to satisfy a generic escort-shortage penalty.
Apply the Branch escort penalty to free availability, maintenance and convoy opportunity cost rather than inventing unnamed losses.
A Branch-saved hull is not automatically free, in-theatre, ready, or at Ceylon. Hermes/Vampire/Hollyhock require their own dated location/readiness trace before counting.
Historical later combat outcomes are not imported as proof of Branch outcomes.

lower_escort_network.role: convoy ASW/minesweeping/local escort across Aden-Bombay-Ceylon-Calcutta-Kilindini routes; not interchangeable with fleet destroyer screen
lower_escort_network.count_policy: Do not convert the representative list into a single Ceylon-ready count. Branch burden is tracked as escort-days/ship-days and free-reserve penalty.
lower_escort_network.Branch_effect: Additional Indian Ocean burden leaves freely assignable destroyer/escort reserve roughly 2-4 hulls worse than historical, even if raw hull count is near historical/slightly higher.

late_Jan_destroyer_screen_interpretation.distribution_note: Not one 11-DD tactical screen: Unicorn+Roebuck+Rapid go Cochin; Renown+Rotherham+Norman go Colombo; remaining units distribute with Trincomalee group; Norman requires repair.
late_Jan_destroyer_screen_interpretation.working_free_screen_band: 5-7 uncommitted/short-notice center ~6; deliberate capital sortie can assemble about 7 and potentially 7-9 only by stripping convoy/ASW/training duties.
late_Jan_destroyer_screen_interpretation.evidence_guard: This is a Branch availability band, not a historical point count. Historical 10 Feb sortie with seven destroyers demonstrates seven can be assembled; diary later explicitly reports escort duties curtailing heavy-ship training.

working_conclusion: January reinforcement is heavy-ship dominated. Medium/light new arrivals are real but narrow: one cruiser, four through destroyers, two submarines. Local destroyers reinforce the passage but are not new theatre arrivals; the cruiser layer remains dispersed and the escort reserve remains constrained.
